questions.question: Which sport is this a close-up from?
questions.explanation: The numbers round the board are jumbled on purpose, so a throw that just misses the 20 lands in the measly 1 or 5.

media.alt: A round target board with three thrown pieces stuck in it

questions.question: Which sport uses these?
questions.explanation: Wearing gloves became part of the rules in 1867, under the Marquess of Queensberry Rules.

media.alt: A pair of padded black gloves
media.credit: Photo: Julieb2768, CC BY-SA 3.0 (Wikimedia Commons)

questions.question: Which sport is this a close-up from?
questions.explanation: The hoop is 10 feet (about 3 metres) off the ground, the same height as when the game was invented in 1891.

media.alt: A hoop with a net, fixed to a see-through board on a pole
media.credit: Photo: Tonniedixon, CC BY-SA 3.0 (Wikimedia Commons)

questions.question: Which sport is this a close-up from?
questions.explanation: The two small pieces of wood balanced on top are the bails: knock one off and the batter could be out.

media.alt: Three wooden posts in the grass, topped with two small pieces of wood
media.credit: Photo: Acabashi, CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikimedia Commons)

questions.question: Which sport uses this ball?
questions.explanation: Early balls like this had a pig's bladder inside a leather case, which helped give them their oval shape.

media.alt: An oval ball covered in signatures
media.credit: Photo: Unknown, CC BY-SA 3.0 (Wikimedia Commons)

questions.question: Which sport uses this?
questions.explanation: The dimples help the ball fly about twice as far as a smooth one would.

media.alt: A small white dimpled ball beside a hole in short grass
media.credit: Photo: Lotus Head from Johannesburg, Gauteng, South Africa, CC BY-SA 3.0 (Wikimedia Commons)

questions.question: Which sport uses these?
questions.explanation: A smash can send one of these flying at over 500 km/h, making it the fastest thing in any racket sport.

media.alt: Feathered objects with rounded cork bases
media.credit: Photo: Arne Nordmann (user:norro), Germany, CC BY-SA 3.0 (Wikimedia Commons)

questions.question: Which sport is this a close-up from?
questions.explanation: Knocking all the pins down with your first ball is a strike, and twelve strikes in a row makes a perfect score of 300.

media.alt: A row of white pins with a ball rolling towards them

questions.question: Which sport is being played here?
questions.explanation: It began as an after-dinner game in Victorian England, sometimes with a row of books as the net.

media.alt: Two players either side of a small table with a net, in a big arena
media.credit: Photo: Pierre-Yves Beaudouin, CC BY-SA 3.0 (Wikimedia Commons)

questions.question: Which sport is this?
questions.explanation: The suits and blades are wired up, so a light comes on and a buzzer sounds when a hit lands.

media.alt: Two people in white suits and masks, one lunging with a thin blade
media.credit: Photo: Marie-Lan Nguyen, CC BY 2.5 (Wikimedia Commons)

questions.question: Which sport uses this racket and ball?
questions.explanation: The ball hardly bounces until it's warm, which is why players hit it about for a few minutes before a match.

media.alt: A racket and a small black ball on a wooden floor

questions.question: Which sport is being played here?
questions.explanation: Players can't touch the bottom of the pool, so they tread water all game with a kick called the eggbeater.

media.alt: Players in caps swimming after a yellow ball beside a goal in a pool
media.credit: Photo: Massimo Finizio, CC BY-SA 2.0 it (Wikimedia Commons)

questions.question: Which sport is this?
questions.explanation: As well as hoops, these gymnasts perform with a ball, clubs and a long ribbon.

media.alt: Five gymnasts in sparkly outfits holding hoops and clubs
media.credit: Photo: Miriam Jeske, CC BY 3.0 br (Wikimedia Commons)

questions.question: Which event is this athlete taking part in?
questions.explanation: The bendy poles are made of fibreglass or carbon fibre, and they can fling the best vaulters over six metres up.

media.alt: An athlete flying upside down over a high bar, with a long bending stick
media.credit: Photo: Unknown, CC BY-SA 3.0 (Wikimedia Commons)

questions.question: Which sport is this?
questions.explanation: Every pole a horse knocks down costs its rider four faults.

media.alt: A rider on a horse leaping over a white fence in front of a crowd
media.credit: Photo: Ronjamin (Ronald C. Yochum Jr.), CC BY 2.5 (Wikimedia Commons)

questions.question: Which sport is this a close-up from?
questions.explanation: Track bikes have a single fixed gear and no brakes at all.

media.alt: Two riders racing on a steeply banked wooden track
media.credit: Photo: Daieuxetdailleurs, CC BY 4.0 (Wikimedia Commons)

questions.question: Which sport is being played here?
questions.explanation: A clean catch from a kick is called a mark, and leaping ones like this are known as 'speccies'.

media.alt: A player leaping high over another to catch an oval red ball
media.credit: Photo: Flickerd, CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikimedia Commons)

questions.question: Which sport is this a close-up from?
questions.explanation: The men's 'hammer' is a metal ball on a steel wire that weighs 7.26 kg, the same as the men's shot.

media.alt: An athlete spinning inside a netted cage, a metal ball flying behind him
media.credit: Photo: Daltoro, CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikimedia Commons)

questions.question: Which sport uses this equipment?
questions.explanation: The All England Club at Wimbledon was founded for this game in 1868, before lawn tennis took over.

media.alt: A mallet, coloured balls and a white hoop on a lawn
media.credit: Photo: Winnywinn, CC BY-SA 3.0 (Wikimedia Commons)

questions.question: Which sport is this a close-up from?
questions.explanation: Until 2017 the sport was officially called synchronised swimming.

media.alt: A swimmer held up out of the water by team-mates in an Olympic pool
media.credit: Photo: Rafael Brais/brasil2016.gov.br, CC BY 3.0 (Wikimedia Commons)

questions.question: Which sport is played with this ball?
questions.explanation: The sliotar has a cork centre, and players can run with it balanced on the flat end of the stick.

media.alt: A small white leather ball with raised stitched ridges
media.credit: Photo: The Grimclaw, CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikimedia Commons)

questions.question: Which martial art is this?
questions.explanation: Kendo fighters strike with a sword made from four slats of bamboo, called a shinai.

media.alt: Two fighters in dark armour and masks, one striking with a long wooden sword
media.credit: Photo: 江戸村のとくぞう, CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikimedia Commons)

questions.question: Which sport is this a close-up from?
questions.explanation: Sliders lie on their backs, feet first, steering with their calves and shoulders at around 140 km/h.

media.alt: Two sliders lying on their backs, feet first, on an icy track
media.credit: Photo: The U.S. Army, CC BY 2.0 (Wikimedia Commons)

questions.question: Which sport is this a close-up from?
questions.explanation: The sport grew out of ski patrols by soldiers, and it has been in the Winter Olympics since 1960.

media.alt: Skiers lying down and standing at a row of targets, holding rifles
media.credit: Photo: Unknown, CC BY-SA 3.0 (Wikimedia Commons)

questions.question: Which sport is this a close-up from?
questions.explanation: In the 3,000 metres steeplechase runners clear 28 barriers and seven water jumps.

media.alt: Runners splashing through a water pit after jumping a barrier
media.credit: Photo: Augustas Didžgalvis, CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikimedia Commons)

questions.question: Which sport is played on this court?
questions.explanation: It was a favourite game of Henry VIII, and his court at Hampton Court Palace is still played on today.

media.alt: A long indoor court with a sloping roofed gallery down one side and a net
media.credit: Photo: Horacio Gomes, CC BY-SA 3.0 (Wikimedia Commons)

questions.question: Which sport is being played here?
questions.explanation: Players hold their breath to push a puck along the pool floor; the game was invented in Southsea in 1954.

media.alt: Swimmers in masks and snorkels pushing a puck along the bottom of a pool
media.credit: Photo: DavidUnderwater, CC BY-SA 3.0 (Wikimedia Commons)

questions.question: Which sport is being played here?
questions.explanation: Its name joins the Malay word for kick, sepak, with the Thai word for the woven ball, takraw.

media.alt: A player flipping upside down to kick a ball over a net
media.credit: Photo: Republic of Korea from Seoul, Republic of Korea, CC BY-SA 2.0 (Wikimedia Commons)

questions.question: Which sport is this?
questions.explanation: Paddlers must pass through hanging gates: green ones heading downstream, red ones heading back upstream.

media.alt: A paddler in a small boat on white water, between hanging poles

questions.question: Which sport is being played here?
questions.explanation: The attacking 'raider' must keep chanting 'kabaddi' on a single breath while trying to tag opponents.

media.alt: A player in white being tackled by a group of opponents on a mat
media.credit: Photo: Amir Hosseini, CC BY 4.0 (Wikimedia Commons)
